cards.name: Automatic Click Remover
cards.summary: Finds and repairs short clicks, pops and crackle automatically (Adobe Audition's restoration algorithm). It treats brief impulses only, not steady hiss or hum.
use_for: Remove mouth clicks and lip smacks from documentary or explainer VO
Clean crackle from archival or vinyl-sourced speeches and old newsreel audio
Repair digital pops from dropouts or bad edits in field interviews
avoid: Low Threshold plus high Complexity dulls consonants and plosives (speech sounds lispy or smeared)
It does nothing for steady hiss, hum or room tone: use Adaptive Noise Reduction or DeHummer
Heavy settings can stutter playback on long clips: render audio previews

params.name: Threshold
params.does: Click detection sensitivity; LOWER catches more clicks but risks treating speech as clicks. Measured: a single full-scale click was removed completely at 0.1, 0.29 and 0.9 (output peak 149 dB below it).
params.typical: UI 1-100, default 30 = normalized 0.293 (inferred (v-1)/99). Light VO declick 30-40 (0.29-0.39); heavy archival crackle 15-25 (0.14-0.24)

params.name: Complexity
params.does: How complex the clicks it tries to repair can be; higher = more processing and more artefacts

cards.scripting: Audio effect: add with the QE audio track item's addAudioEffect(qe.project.getAudioEffectByName('Automatic Click Remover')), then set values on the DOM component (the harvest found it as the LAST component of the audio TrackItem). Every audio-effect property reads and writes NORMALIZED 0..1 (the harvest clamped to 0..1), not UI units; the (v-1)/99 mapping for Threshold/Complexity is inferred from the Audition defaults 30/16, so read back once to confirm. Ignore 'IsProcessing' and 'Reset' (internal) and the unnamed bool row. pr_build.jsx addFx only adds VIDEO effects today, so an audio-effect path is needed. Set once; do not keyframe.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: DeHummer
cards.summary: Removes electrical hum (mains frequency and its harmonics) with a comb of narrow notch filters. Frequency, notch width, depth and number of harmonics are adjustable.
use_for: Remove 50 Hz mains hum from Indian field interviews, press-conference feeds and rally recordings
Clean ground-loop buzz from a camera or mixer XLR feed
Fix hum on archival broadcast clips before using them in a documentary
avoid: Wrong base frequency: India runs on 50 Hz mains; the default is believed to be 60 Hz (US), so it can miss Indian hum entirely. Always set the base frequency explicitly (after calibrating the normalized value)
Too many harmonics or too low a Q (wide notches) thins out male voices and music bass
Leaving Output Hum Only on renders only the removed hum

params.name: Harmonic Base Frequency
params.does: Root hum frequency the notches are built on
params.typical: 50 Hz for India/Europe, 60 Hz for US sources. Harvest default 0.002002 is believed to be 60 Hz but the normalized scale is NOT verified: calibrate once (set 50 Hz in the UI, read the value back) before scripting

params.name: Harmonic Base Q
params.does: Width of the root notch and its harmonics; higher Q = narrower, less tonal damage

params.name: Harmonic Base Gain
params.does: Depth of the hum cut. Measured on 50 Hz hum with harmonics: 0 cuts about 13 dB overall, the default 0.235 about 5 dB, 1 nothing, so lower = deeper cut (confirmed).
params.typical: default 0.235 (about -5 dB on hum); 0-0.1 for a deep cut (about -13 dB)

params.name: Num Harmonics
params.does: How many harmonics above the root are notched
params.typical: default 1.0 (the harvested maximum); reduce if voices get thin

params.name: Harmonic Slope
params.does: Attenuation of higher harmonics relative to the root

params.name: Output Hum Only
params.does: 0 = cleaned audio, 1 = monitor only what is removed

cards.equivalent: Parametric EQ (AE, manual narrow cuts only)
cards.scripting: Audio effect: QE addAudioEffect on the audio track item, then set the DOM component (last component on the TrackItem). Values are normalized 0..1; UI units for frequency, Q and gain could not be derived from the harvest (only defaults are known), so a script should either keep defaults or use values calibrated by a read-back from the UI. Ignore the unnamed bool row. Set once; no keyframes.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Parametric Equalizer
cards.summary: Audition's full parametric EQ: low and high shelves, five peaking bands, plus switchable high-pass and low-pass filters and an output gain. The workhorse tone-shaping tool for VO, music and SFX.
use_for: VO cleanup: high-pass rumble below ~80 Hz and cut boxiness around 250-400 Hz
Add presence (+2-4 dB around 3-5 kHz) so explainer VO cuts through a music bed
Carve a dip in the music bed where the voice sits
Telephone / walkie-talkie / archival radio voice: high-pass ~300 Hz + low-pass ~3.4 kHz
Muffled-to-clear reveal on a trailer hit by sweeping the low-pass cutoff
avoid: Big boosts (>6 dB) raise noise and clip; cut before you boost and lower 'Gain' if you boost
Narrow, high-gain boosts ring and whistle
Frequency mapping is inferred, not verified: listen or read back before trusting exact Hz

params.name: High-Pass Filter Enable
params.does: Turns the high-pass (rumble) filter on (1) or off (0)

params.name: High-Pass Cutoff Frequency
params.does: High-pass corner frequency
params.typical: VO 70-100 Hz = 0.003-0.004 on the measured 24 000 x v scale (if HP shares it)

params.name: EQ Band 2 Center Frequency
params.does: Band 2 centre (default 0.01126, about 270 Hz on the measured scale): mud / boxiness area

params.name: EQ Band 2 Gain
params.does: Band 2 gain; 0.5 = 0 dB, below 0.5 cuts, above boosts (+-48 dB range, about 0.0104 per dB, measured on Band 3)
params.typical: 0.45-0.48 for a gentle mud cut on VO

params.name: EQ Band 4 Center Frequency
params.does: Band 4 centre (default 0.199, about 4.8 kHz on the measured scale): presence / intelligibility

params.name: EQ Band 4 Gain
params.does: Band 4 gain; 0.5 = 0 dB
params.typical: 0.52-0.55 for a gentle presence lift on VO

params.name: Low-Pass Filter Enable
params.does: Turns the low-pass filter on (1) or off (0)

params.name: Low-Pass Cutoff Frequency
params.does: Low-pass corner frequency (default 1.0 = top of the range)
params.typical: telephone 3.4 kHz = 0.142; through-a-wall 500 Hz = 0.021 (if LP shares the measured scale)

params.name: EQ Band 3 Gain
params.does: Band 3 gain (default 0.5 = 0 dB). Measured: 0.5 = 0 dB, 0.75 = +23.7 dB, 1 = +35.6 dB (third-octave readings), which fits a +/-48 dB band range (about 0.0104 per dB); cuts show only as a notch, not in this boost reading.
params.typical: 0.475-0.48 for a gentle 2-2.5 dB cut, 0.52-0.53 for a 2-3 dB lift

params.name: EQ Band 3 Center Frequency
params.does: Band 3 centre (default 0.0426, about 1 kHz). Measured: linear in Hz, 0.01 = 250 Hz, 0.05 = 1.26 kHz, 0.2 = 5 kHz, 0.5 = 12.7 kHz (third-octave readings, so the scale is 22 600-28 100 Hz per unit; 24 000 x v fits every reading). The default-derived 25 + 19975 v reads about a fifth low.

measured.figure: band of the largest boost (Hz, third-octave resolution)

cards.scripting: Audio effect: QE addAudioEffect on the audio track item, then set the DOM component (last on the TrackItem). All values normalized 0..1. Frequency rows are linear in Hz (measured on EQ Band 3 Center Frequency: about 24 000 x v Hz, 0.01 = 250 Hz, 0.05 = 1.26 kHz, 0.2 = 5 kHz; the earlier default-derived 25 + 19975 v reads about a fifth low); HP/LP cutoffs presumably share it (not measured). Gains: 0.5 = 0 dB for shelves and bands; measured on Band 3: 0.75 = +23.7 dB, 1 = +35.6 dB, which fits the +-48 dB range (about 0.0104 per dB), so keep moves small; master 'Gain' 0.6667 = 0 dB. Q and Bandwidth scales unknown: leave them. Telephone voice (300 Hz-3.4 kHz on the measured scale) = {High-Pass Filter Enable: 1, High-Pass Cutoff Frequency: 0.0125, Low-Pass Filter Enable: 1, Low-Pass Cutoff Frequency: 0.142}. Bands are enabled at 0 dB by default, so untouched bands are neutral. Ignore Bypass, LowGraphRange, Original Sample Rate, Ultra-Quiet Mode and the unnamed bool. The recipe (muffled-to-clear reveal) needs Low-Pass Filter Enable = 1 first; it has a middle key at 0.1 (~2 kHz) because the frequency scale is linear in Hz, so a straight 0.024 -> 1 ramp would spend almost all its time above 3 kHz.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Adaptive Noise Reduction
cards.summary: Learns the steady background noise (hiss, fan, AC, traffic wash) on the fly and reduces it, without a noise print. Strong settings cause watery, bubbly artefacts.
use_for: Reduce fan, AC or laptop hiss under home-recorded explainer VO
Clean steady background wash from field interviews and press-conference audio
Tidy noisy archival clips before mixing under narration
avoid: Pushing Reduce Noise By too far makes voices underwater / bubbly
It adapts over time: the first moments of a clip may be untreated, so leave a little room tone at the head
Not for clicks or hum (use Automatic Click Remover / DeHummer); for heavy noise the newer DeNoise or Essential Sound Enhance Speech may do better

params.name: Reduce Noise By
params.does: Amount of noise reduction (Adobe suggests 6-30 dB in the UI). Measured on pink noise: 0 = no change, 0.5 = -4.9 dB, 1 = -5.1 dB (it levels off).
params.typical: default 0.5; gentle VO cleanup 0.3-0.5, lower if voices turn watery (measured: 0.5 = -4.9 dB, 1 = -5.1 dB on pink noise)

params.name: Noisiness
params.does: Estimated share of the audio that is noise (UI %)

params.name: Fine Tune Noise Floor
params.does: Shifts the auto-detected noise floor up or down

params.name: Signal Threshold
params.does: Shifts the auto-detected threshold of wanted audio

params.name: Spectral Decay Rate
params.does: How fast processing falls off; too short = bubbly, too long = reverby

params.name: Broadband Preservation
params.does: Protects audio near detected artefacts; lower removes more noise but sounds processed

params.name: High Quality Mode (slower)
params.does: Higher-quality, slower processing (0/1)

cards.scripting: Audio effect: QE addAudioEffect on the audio track item, then set the DOM component (last on the TrackItem). All values normalized 0..1; only defaults are known, the UI-unit scales (dB, ms, Hz) are unverified except Noisiness which reads as a percentage. Ignore 'Is Processing' and the unnamed bool. Put it FIRST in a VO chain (before EQ and compression). Adds latency and CPU load; do not keyframe.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Amplify
cards.summary: Boosts or cuts the level of the clip by a fixed amount, with a gain slider per channel (linked by default).
use_for: Bring a quiet interview or phone recording up before compression
Level-match clips from different sources in a news compilation
Pre-gain a whisper or SFX before other effects in the chain
avoid: Big boosts on already-loud clips clip the output: add a Hard Limiter after it
Simple level changes are easier on the clip's own Volume > Level (pr_build gain_db already does this)

params.name: Gain
params.does: Master gain for all channels when Link Sliders is on. Measured on a stereo clip: 'Gain' does not exist there (setting it found no such property and the level did not change); a stereo Amplify exposes 'Left' and 'Right' sliders instead (pve/harvest/pr_audio_params_w3.json).
params.typical: 0.6667 = 0 dB. If the scale is -96..+48 dB (fits the default but unverified), 1 dB = 0.00694: +3 dB = 0.6875, +6 dB = 0.7083, -6 dB = 0.625

params.name: Link Sliders
params.does: 1 = per-channel sliders follow Gain together

cards.scripting: Audio effect: QE addAudioEffect on the audio track item, then set the DOM component (last on the TrackItem). Normalized 0..1 values. The 32 unnamed rows are per-channel gain sliders (all 0.6667 = 0 dB) and cannot be addressed by name; with Link Sliders = 1 setting 'Gain' is enough on a MONO clip. On a stereo clip the component has no 'Gain': it exposes 'Left' and 'Right' (stereo dump, live wave 3), setting 'Gain' there fails ('no such property') and changes nothing, so set Left and Right (their dB scale is not measured; 0.6667 = 0 dB by the default). 'Channel Count' (1/32 for the mono test clip) and 'Link Keyframes' are bookkeeping: do not set. Keyframes on Gain work but clip Volume keyframes are the normal way to ride levels.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Analog Delay
cards.summary: Echo modelled on tape, tube and analog delay units: repeats of the sound with warm, slightly dirty colouring. Delay time, feedback, wet/dry mix and saturation are adjustable.
use_for: Echo on a trailer title hit or last word of a line ('...forever ... forever')
Slapback on a satire stinger or meme SFX
Dreamy / flashback treatment of a quote in a documentary
Rhythmic echo on music stings in reels
avoid: Echo on running narration hurts intelligibility; use only on isolated words or SFX
High Feedback builds up into runaway self-oscillation
Echo tails get cut at the clip's out point: extend the clip or put it on a track/nest

params.name: Delay
params.does: Time between repeats. Measured: the first echo comes 8 x value seconds after the dry sound (0.01 = 0.09 s, 0.0238 = 0.20 s, 0.1 = 0.81 s, 0.3 = 2.4 s), i.e. ms = 10 + 7990 v as inferred; each echo about 16 dB below the dry signal at the default Wet / Dry Out.
params.typical: measured linear ms = 10 + 7990*n (default 200 ms = 0.0238). Slapback 80-120 ms = 0.0088-0.0138; trailer echo 300-500 ms = 0.0363-0.0613

params.name: Feedback
params.does: How much of each echo is fed back (number and decay of repeats)
params.typical: default 0.1; 0.2-0.4 for a decaying echo; keep below 0.5 (if the range is Audition's 0-200%, 0.5 = 100% = endless repeats)

params.name: Wet Out
params.does: Level of the echoed signal

params.name: Dry Out
params.does: Level of the original signal

params.name: Trash
params.does: Adds distortion and low-end warmth to the repeats

params.name: Spread
params.does: Stereo width of the repeats

params.name: Mode
params.does: Delay-unit character: Tape / Tape-Tube / Analog

cards.scripting: Audio effect: QE addAudioEffect on the audio track item, then set the DOM component (last on the TrackItem). Normalized 0..1 values. Delay scale measured (ms = 10 + 7990 v: 0.0238 = 0.20 s, 0.1 = 0.81 s); Dry/Wet read as 0..1 = 0..100%. Mode is a 3-item dropdown in normalized space (0, 0.5, 1): order Tape, Tape/Tube, Analog is from Audition docs, not verified by harvest. For a single echoed word, cut that word to its own clip and apply the delay there, with tail room after it.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Channel Mixer
cards.summary: Routes and mixes the input channels into each output channel (L to L, R to L, L to R ... up to 8 channels): swap, fold to mono, invert one side or blend left and right on a stereo or multichannel clip.
use_for: Interview recorded with the lav on one channel only: send it to both sides
Swap or blend channels on a stereo camera track
Use only the clean channel of a dual-channel camera recording when the other mic is noisy or distorted
avoid: It needs a stereo (or multichannel) clip; on the mono harvest clip it did not attach at all
For a whole-clip fix, Modify > Audio Channels or Fill Left with Right / Fill Right with Left is simpler

params.name: Channel Count
params.does: Channel count of the mixer (bookkeeping; the stereo default is 0.25). Measured: no audible change at 0 / 0.5 / 1.

measured.signal: a split stereo pair (L 440 Hz at -12 dBFS, R 1 kHz at -24 dBFS)

params.name: L to L
params.does: Share of the left input in the left output. Measured: bipolar, 0 = -100 % (the left input at full level, polarity inverted), 0.5 = 0 % (silent), 1 = +100 % (unchanged, the default): v = 0.5 + 0.5 x gain.

measured.signal: a split stereo pair (L 440 Hz at -12 dBFS, R 1 kHz at -24 dBFS)

params.name: R to L
params.does: share of the right input in the left output, bipolar like L to L (0.5 = 0 %, the default)
params.typical: 0.75 + L to L 0.75 to fold both into the left at -6 dB each

params.name: L to R
params.does: share of the left input in the right output (0.5 = 0 %, the default)

params.name: R to R
params.does: share of the right input in the right output (1 = +100 %, the default)

cards.scripting: Stereo / multichannel clips only: on a mono clip it does not attach (the 2026-10-03 mono harvest read the clip Volume row instead; the batch now holds the stereo dump from pve/harvest/pr_audio_params_w3.json, match c5ca9e29-df07-42a6-8800-ba80324e5cbc). Properties '<input> to <output>' for inputs L, R, 3..8 and outputs L, R, 3..8 (64 rows) plus 'Channel Count'. Every amount is bipolar: v = 0.5 + 0.5 x gain, so 0 = -100 % (full level, polarity inverted), 0.5 = 0 % (silent), 1 = +100 %; the defaults (L to L 1, R to R 1, everything else 0.5) pass the clip unchanged (measured on a split stereo pair, live wave 3). Mono fold: L to L 0.75, R to L 0.75, L to R 0.75, R to R 0.75 (each input at 50 %). Apply with QE addAudioEffect and check that the last component's displayName is 'Channel Mixer'.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Chorus/Flanger
cards.summary: Modulated short delays in one effect: chorus thickens a sound into several slightly detuned voices, flanger sweeps a hollow jet-plane comb filter. Mode picks which.
use_for: Robotic / AI voice texture for AI-education explainers (sparingly)
Dream or flashback swirl on SFX and music stings
Thicken a synth riser or drone in a trailer
Whooshy sweep on a transition SFX
avoid: On running news or documentary narration it sounds cheap and seasick
High Intensity on full mixes smears the music

params.name: Mode
params.does: Chorus or Flanger (2-item switch, 0 or 1)
params.typical: default 1 (= Flanger if the UI order Chorus, Flanger holds; not verified, listen once)

params.name: Speed
params.does: LFO rate of the delay sweep

params.name: Width
params.does: Maximum delay depth of the sweep

params.name: Intensity
params.does: Ratio of processed to original sound. Measured on pink noise: +1.4 dB at 0, +1.8 dB at 0.5, +3.9 dB at 1 with comb ripple up to 9.5 dB; at its defaults it raises a tone by 5.8 dB.

params.name: Transience
params.does: Emphasizes transients for a sharper, more distinct sound

cards.scripting: Audio effect: QE addAudioEffect on the audio track item, then set the DOM component (last on the TrackItem). Normalized 0..1 values; UI units unknown beyond the defaults. Defaults are already clearly audible. Mode is a 2-way switch in normalized space (0 / 1) with unverified labels (enum_labels assume the UI order Chorus, Flanger).

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Convolution Reverb
cards.summary: Places audio in a real space by convolving it with an impulse response (rooms, halls, churches, plates); the space is chosen from a built-in Impulse list.
use_for: Match a clean studio VO or ADR line to the on-screen room in a documentary
Big hall tail on trailer impacts and title slams
Make a quote sound as if spoken in a hall, parliament or rally ground
Memory / flashback voice treatment
Glue foley and SFX into a scene
avoid: Reverb on main narration kills intelligibility; keep VO dry or barely wet
Harvest default Mix is 1.0 (maximum): always set Mix explicitly
Tails are cut at the clip out point: extend the clip or apply on a track / nested sequence

params.name: Impulse
params.does: Which built-in impulse response (space) to use, stepped dropdown in normalized space

params.name: Mix
params.does: Wet/dry balance. Measured on a click with the default impulse: decay T30 0 s at 0, 0.15 s at 0.5, 0.16 s at 1 (a short room).
params.typical: subtle room on VO 0.1-0.25; trailer hit tail 0.4-0.7

params.name: Room Size
params.does: Scales the impulse length (size of the space)

params.name: Damping HF
params.does: Darkens the tail by cutting high frequencies

params.name: Damping LF
params.does: Cuts low-frequency build-up in the tail (less boom/mud)

params.name: Pre-Delay
params.does: Time the reverb takes to build to full level: 0-10 ms sounds natural, 50 ms or more is a special effect
params.typical: 0 default; small values for big spaces

params.name: Width
params.does: Stereo width of the tail (default 0.333 likely = 100%)

params.name: Gain
params.does: Output gain (default 0.4167, assumed 0 dB)

cards.scripting: Audio effect: QE addAudioEffect on the audio track item, then set the DOM component (last on the TrackItem). Normalized 0..1 values; percent controls (Mix, Room Size) read as 0..1 = 0..100%, the rest only by default. Impulse is a list index stored in normalized form: stepping it blindly picks an unknown space. Convolution is CPU-heavier than Studio Reverb; render audio previews. Recipe = reverb throw: the line stays nearly dry, then the last word (from ~1.0 s, shift to the word) blooms into the space; leave tail room after the clip.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: DeEsser
cards.summary: Frequency-targeted compressor that turns down harsh sibilance ('s', 'sh', 'ch') in voices when it crosses a threshold.
use_for: Tame harsh esses on close-miked documentary or explainer VO
Smooth sibilant AI / TTS voiceover lines
Fix sibilance made worse by a presence EQ boost or heavy compression
Soften harsh field-interview mics
avoid: Over-de-essing makes speakers sound lispy
Leaving Output Sibilance Only on renders only the hiss band

params.name: Threshold
params.does: Level above which sibilance is reduced; LOWER = more de-essing. Measured on pink noise: 0.25 cuts the sibilance band by up to 12 dB (-0.6 dB overall), the default 0.625 by up to 2 dB, 1 does nothing: lower = more de-essing (confirmed).

params.name: Center Frequency
params.does: Centre of the sibilance band
params.typical: default 0.391; male VO ~4-6 kHz, female ~6-8 kHz in the UI (normalized scale unverified)

params.name: Bandwidth
params.does: Width of the band that is detected and reduced

params.name: Mode
params.does: Broadband (whole signal ducks) or Multiband (only the sibilance band)
params.typical: default 1 (= Multiband if the UI order Broadband, Multiband holds; not verified)

params.name: Output Sibilance Only
params.does: 1 = monitor only the detected sibilance

params.name: Attack
params.does: How fast reduction starts

params.name: Release
params.does: How fast reduction recovers

cards.scripting: Audio effect: QE addAudioEffect on the audio track item, then set the DOM component (last on the TrackItem). Normalized 0..1 values; only defaults are known. Place after noise reduction and EQ, before or after the compressor. Set once, no keyframes.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Distortion
cards.summary: Waveshaping distortion: an amplitude transfer curve (drawn on positive and negative graphs in the UI) clips and bends the waveform for grit, fuzz or a broken-speaker sound.
use_for: Megaphone / rally loudspeaker voice (with a band-limiting Parametric Equalizer)
Walkie-talkie or radio-intercept voice in trailers
Gritty glitch stingers and meme SFX in satire reels
avoid: The transfer curves are NOT exposed to scripting, so a script cannot set how hard it distorts
On full mixes or narration it sounds harsh and cheap
Distortion raises level: follow with Hard Limiter

params.name: Positive Smoothing
params.does: Curve smoothing of the positive-sample graph

params.name: Negative Smoothing
params.does: Curve smoothing of the negative-sample graph

params.name: Time Smoothing
params.does: How quickly distortion reacts to level changes

params.name: dB Range
params.does: Amplitude range the graphs cover (limits distortion to that range). Measured on a 1 kHz tone: THD 1.6 % at 0.333, 0.76 % at the default 0.667, 1.3 % at 1; at its defaults it also raises the level by 10.8 dB.

params.name: Symmetric
params.does: 1 = negative curve mirrors the positive one

params.name: Post-Filter DC Offset
params.does: Removes DC offset introduced by asymmetric curves

cards.scripting: Audio effect: QE addAudioEffect on the audio track item, then set the DOM component (last on the TrackItem). Normalized 0..1 values. Only smoothing / range / mode switches are exposed; the curve points live in a custom graph that the harvest did not list, and the default curve distorts mildly but loudly (measured on a 1 kHz tone: +10.8 dB, THD 0.76 %). For scripted grit prefer GuitarSuite ('Dist Amount' is numeric) with a band-limiting Parametric Equalizer; a configured instance saved as an effect preset in the UI is an option only if preset application from script is proven. 'Linear Scale' switches the graphs between dB and normalized scales; leave 0.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Dynamics Processing
cards.summary: Audition's graph-based dynamics processor: a drawn input-to-output level curve makes it a compressor, limiter, expander or noise gate, with separate level-detector and gain-processor timing.
use_for: Even out VO level before the final limiter
Gate room noise between sentences in an interview
Squash a music bed so it sits steadily under narration
Punch up trailer hits and SFX
avoid: Default curve is a straight line (no processing): it does nothing until the curve is changed
Fast attack/release on music pumps audibly
Curve point scale is not verified; Single-band Compressor or Hard Limiter are easier to script, and Dynamics (AutoGate section) is the scriptable gate

params.name: Number of X/Y Pairs
params.does: How many curve points are active, out of 7 (default 3/7 = 0.4286)

params.name: Location2
params.does: Input level of curve point 2 (the knee); default 0.8
params.typical: 0.8 (believed -20 dBFS if the axis is -100..0 dB)

params.name: Value2
params.does: Output level of curve point 2
params.typical: same as Location2 for no gain change at the knee

params.name: Value3
params.does: Output level at full-scale input (Location3 = 1); below 1 compresses above the knee
params.typical: 0.85 for roughly 4:1 above -20 dB on the assumed axis

params.name: Make-Up Gain
params.does: Gain added after processing
params.typical: default 0; raise a little after compressing

params.name: Gain Processor - Attack Time
params.does: How fast gain reduction engages

params.name: Gain Processor - Release Time
params.does: How fast gain reduction recovers

params.name: Peak/RMS
params.does: Level detector reacts to peaks or average (RMS) level
params.typical: 1 default (likely RMS, unverified); RMS suits VO

params.name: Output Gain
params.does: Gain after the transfer curve (default 0.5 = 0 dB). Measured: 0.25 = -24 dB, 0.5 = 0 dB, 0.75 = +20 dB (not quite symmetric).

cards.scripting: Audio effect: QE addAudioEffect on the audio track item, then set the DOM component (last on the TrackItem). Normalized 0..1 values. The transfer curve is Location1..7 (input) / Value1..7 (output) with 'Number of X/Y Pairs' points active; defaults (0,0) (0.8,0.8) (1,1) = unity. The dB meaning of the axis is assumed (-100..0 dB linear), not verified: confirm with a read-back in the UI before relying on thresholds. Ignore 'Current Tab' (UI page), 'Envelope Only', 'Spline Curves' unless needed, 'Noise Gating (if expanding more than 50:1)' (only for gate curves), 'Lock Filter', Low/High Cutoff (side-chain band, default full range).

cards.name: FFT Filter
cards.summary: Draw-a-curve filter: an FFT-based gain-vs-frequency graph built from up to 128 X/Y points, good for very steep notches, band-passes and telephone or radio shapes.
use_for: Steep notch for a single whine or tone in an interview
Telephone / radio / walkie-talkie voice with brick-wall edges
Remove everything below a frequency for a thin archival feel
avoid: Large FFT sizes smear transients (pre-echo, ringing)
Point coordinates are hard to place blind; Parametric Equalizer is easier to script for normal EQ

params.name: Number of X/Y pairs
params.does: How many curve points are active, out of 128 (default 2/128 = 0.015625)

params.name: X 1
params.does: Frequency of point 1 (normalized)

params.name: Y 1
params.does: Gain of point 1; 0.75 is the flat default (inferred 0 dB). Measured on pink noise (point 1 moved, point 2 left at 0.75): 0.25 = -16.5 dB overall, 0.75 = flat (+0.8), 1 = +14.9 dB, so 0.75 = 0 dB (confirmed).

params.name: X 2
params.does: Frequency of point 2

params.name: Y 2
params.does: Gain of point 2

params.name: Splines
params.does: 0 = straight segments between points, 1 = smooth curve

params.name: FFT Size
params.does: Frequency resolution vs time smearing

cards.scripting: Audio effect: QE addAudioEffect on the audio track item, then set the DOM component (last on the TrackItem). Normalized 0..1 values. The graph is X n / Y n points (n = 1..128) with 'Number of X/Y pairs' = count/128; points must be in rising X order. Default is a flat line (0.00125, 0.75) to (1, 0.75). The Hz meaning of X depends on 'Scale' (0 default, probably log vs linear) and Frequency Start/End; Y = 0.75 = 0 dB is measured (0.25 = -16.5 dB, 1 = +14.9 dB overall when point 1 moves). Window Type, Lock, Gain Start/End: leave defaults.

cards.name: Flanger
cards.summary: Audition's flanger: mixes the sound with a copy whose short delay sweeps between an initial and a final time, giving the classic jet-plane whoosh and metallic comb sweep.
use_for: Jet-sweep on a transition whoosh or riser in trailers
Sci-fi / AI / hologram voice tag in AI-education reels (short lines only)
Psychedelic flashback or dream treatment on music
Glitchy satire stinger
avoid: On narration it sounds cheap and tiring
High Feedback becomes harsh and ringing

params.name: Mix
params.does: Ratio of flanged to original sound. Measured on pink noise: 0.4 = -4.5 dB overall with comb notches to -10 dB, 1 = -2.5 dB; at its defaults a tone drops 4 dB.

params.name: Feedback
params.does: How much flanged signal is fed back (resonance, metallic edge)

params.name: Initial Delay Time
params.does: Delay at the start of the sweep

params.name: Final Delay Time
params.does: Delay at the end of the sweep (sweep depth)

params.name: Modulation Rate (Frequency)
params.does: Sweep speed in Hz (used when not synced to beats)

params.name: Stereo Phasing
params.does: Offset between left and right sweeps (UI degrees; default 0.0778 likely 28 of 360)

params.name: Inverted Mode
params.does: Inverts the delayed copy for a hollower sound

params.name: Sinusoidal Mode
params.does: Sweep follows a sine curve instead of a linear ramp

cards.scripting: Audio effect: QE addAudioEffect on the audio track item, then set the DOM component (last on the TrackItem). Normalized 0..1 values; only defaults known. 'Special Effects Mode' mixes normal and inverted flanging; 'Modulation Rate (Beats)' is the tempo-synced rate. Keyframing Mix gives a one-off whoosh on a transition.
